sentences.text: Heard the parties and perused the case diary.

6. The main offender Ajay Kumar Singh has committed suicide and he has also alleged that some persons have taken the undue advantage and received the money but insisting to pay more and on these circumstances, the deceased has committed suicide.

From the case diary, it is clear that the main offender was Ajay Kumar Singh and his family members i.e. this applicant and Rajan Singh were cooperating in the business but one point in the case is important that when the victim asked that if something happens to Ajay Kumar Singh what will be of their money, then Ajay Kumar Singh had disclosed that he has insurance of Rs.2 crore and by selling his property, his brother, sister and wife will repay the amount of investors, thus, it is clear that the investors were clearly making responsible to Ajay Kumar Singh and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:514 3 MCRC-53635-2025 on the assurance of Ajay Kumar Singh, the money was invested.
7. Looking to all these factors, no purpose would be served by keeping the applicant behind the Bars,

coupled with the fact that trial will take time to be concluded, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.

9. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
10.
Accordingly, Misc. Criminal Case stands disposed of. C.C. as per rules.
(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE DPS Ravendra Singh @ Guddu Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149877725/
